# A spatial multi-omic portrait of survival outcome for clear cell renal cell carcinoma, Meyer et al., 2026

**DISCLAIMER**: The study is currently undergoing peer-review. Therefore, the code base is under active development. It includes code for all data presented in the manuscript but also exploratory data analysis parts. File paths have to be adjusted by the user. 

# Software requirements
```{r}
#Data containers
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(SingleCellExperiment)

#Data processing
library(CATALYST)
library(scuttle)
library(scater)
library(imcRtools)

#Data visualization
library(cytomapper)
library(dittoSeq)

#Utilities
library(tidyverse)

library(stringr)
library(patchwork)
library(BiocParallel)
library(tiff)
```


## Overview
1. Reading in the data
2. Quality control 
3. (Optional) pixel binning
4. "Debarcoding" for pixel assignment
5. Pixel selection for spillover matrix estimation
6. Spillover matrix generation
7. Saving the results
8. Single-cell compensation
9. Image compensation


## Generate the spillover matrix

### Read in the data

```{r read-txts-transform, message=FALSE}
sce_spill <- readSCEfromTXT("/mnt/central_nas/users/marllu/T_panel/spillover/CompensationTcell_unzipped/CompensationTcell", pattern=".txt$")

#Transformation
assay(sce_spill, "exprs") <- asinh(counts(sce_spill)/5)
```



### Quality control

In the next step, we will observe the median pixel intensities per spot and
threshold on medians < 200 counts.
These types of visualization serve two purposes:

1. Small median pixel intensities (< 200 counts) might hinder the robust
estimation of the channel spillover. In that case, consecutive pixels can be
summed (see [Optional pixel binning](#pixel_binning)).

2. Each spotted metal (row) should show the highest median pixel intensity in its
corresponding channel (column). If this is not the case, either the naming of the
.txt files was incorrect or the incorrect metal was spotted.

```{r QC-heatmap, message = FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=7}
# Log10 median pixel counts per spot and channel
plotSpotHeatmap(sce_spill)

# Thresholded on 200 pixel counts
plotSpotHeatmap(sce_spill, log = FALSE, threshold = 200)
```


### Filtering incorrectly assigned pixels

Based on the intensity distribution of all channel, pixels are assigned to their corresponding barcode; here this is the already known metal spot. This procedure serves the purpose to identify pixels that cannot be robustly assigned to the spotted metal. Pixels of such kind can be regarded as "noisy", "background" or "artefacts" that should be removed prior to spillover estimation.

The general workflow for pixel debarcoding is as follows:
1. assign a preliminary metal mass to each pixel
2. for each pixel, estimate a cutoff parameter for the distance between 
positive and negative pixel sets
3. apply the estimated cutoffs to identify truly positive pixels

```{r debarcoding, message=FALSE}
bc_key <- as.numeric(unique(sce_spill$sample_mass))
bc_key <- bc_key[order(bc_key)]

#Preliminary metal mass for pixel
sce_spill <- assignPrelim(sce_spill, bc_key = bc_key)

#estimate and apply cut-offs
sce_spill <- estCutoffs(sce_spill)
sce_spill <- applyCutoffs(sce_spill)
```


The obtained `SingleCellExperiment` now contains the additional `bc_id` entry.
For each pixel, this vector indicates the assigned mass (e.g. `161`) or
`0`, meaning unassigned. 

This information can be visualized in form of a heatmap:

```{r assignment-heatmap, fig.width=7, fig.height=7}
cur_table <- table(sce_spill$bc_id, sce_spill$sample_mass)

pheatmap(log10(cur_table + 1),
         cluster_rows = FALSE,
         cluster_cols = FALSE)

# Compute the fraction of unassigned pixels per spot
cur_table["0",] / colSums(cur_table)
```


```{r pixel-filtering}
# Number of assigned pixels per spot 
spotted_per_channel <- colData(sce_spill) %>% as.data.frame() %>% group_by(bc_id) %>% count(sample_mass) %>% filter(bc_id != 0)

# Filter pixels
# sce_spill <- filterPixels(sce_spill, minevents = 40, correct_pixels = TRUE) spotted_per_channel > 92
```


### Compute spillover matrix

Based on the single-positive pixels, we use the `CATALYST::computeSpillmat()`
function to compute the spillover matrix and `CATALYST::plotSpillmat()` to
visualize it. The `plotSpillmat` function checks the spotted and acquired
metal isotopes against a pre-defined `CATALYST::isotope_list()`.

```{r compute-spillover, fig.width=7, fig.height=7, warning=FALSE}
sce_spill <- computeSpillmat(sce_spill)

#Plot both spillover matrices
plotSpillmat(sce_spill)

# Save spillover matrix in variable
sm <- metadata(sce_spill)$spillover_matrix

# Check that spillover matrices contain are metals that are included in the study
panel <- read.csv("/mnt/central_nas/users/marllu/T_panel/panel.csv")
channels <- paste0(panel$channel[panel$keep == 1], "Di")

channels[!channels %in% rownames(sm)] #Not spotted but included in panel (Iridium channel, Xe, Ba)

rownames(sm)[which(!rownames(sm) %in% channels)] #Spotted but not included in panel 0
```

### Save spillover matrix as csv

Next, we will write out the spillover matrix as .csv file.

```{r write_sm_csv}
write.csv(sm, "/mnt/central_nas/users/marllu/T_panel/spillover/spillover_matrix.csv")
```


## Single-cell data compensation

Firstly, we will use the `CATALYST` package to perform spillover compensation on the
**single-cell mean intensities** using the `compCytof`function.
Load `SpatialExperiment` object generated in previous script.

```{r single-cell-compensation}
sce <- readRDS("/mnt/central_nas/users/marllu/T_panel/data_analysis/sce_01.rds")
sm <- read.csv("/mnt/central_nas/users/marllu/T_panel/spillover/spillover_matrix.csv", row.names = 1)

rowData(sce)$channel_name <- paste0(rowData(sce)$channel, "Di")

sce <- compCytof(sce, sm, 
                 transform = TRUE, cofactor = 1,
                 overwrite = FALSE)

sm
```



To check the effect of channel spillover compensation, the expression of markers
that are affected by spillover can be visualized in form of scatter plots before and after
compensation. Here we focus on oxidative spillover between La139(panCK) and Gd155(CD279)

```{r visualize-single-cell-spillover, message=FALSE}
#Simple scatterplot

# afected by spillover: 162/163 (CD45RO/ FOXP3), 171/172 (Tbet/CD31), 145/146 (4-1BB/CD68)

before <- dittoScatterPlot(sce, x.var = "CD68", y.var = "4-1BB",
                           assay.x = "exprs", assay.y = "exprs") +
    ggtitle("Before compensation")

after <- dittoScatterPlot(sce, x.var = "CD68", y.var = "4-1BB",
                          assay.x = "compexprs", assay.y = "compexprs") +
    ggtitle("After compensation")

before+after

ggsave(plot=before+after, path=, "/mnt/central_nas/users/marllu/T_panel/data_analysis/02_spill_cor/compensation_4-1BB145_CD68146.png", width = 12, height = 6)

#Smoothed density scatterplot
buylrd = c("#313695", "#4575B4", "#74ADD1", "#ABD9E9", "#E0F3F8", "#FFFFBF",
           "#FEE090", "#FDAE61", "#F46D43", "#D73027", "#A50026") 
myColRamp = colorRampPalette(c(buylrd))

smoothScatter(x=assay(sce,"exprs")[rownames(sce) == "CD45RO"],
              y=assay(sce,"exprs")[rownames(sce) == "FOXP3"],
              colramp=myColRamp,
              main="Before compensation")

smoothScatter(x=assay(sce,"compexprs")[rownames(sce) == "CD45RO"],
              y=assay(sce,"compexprs")[rownames(sce) == "FOXP3"],
              colramp=myColRamp,
              main="After compensation")
```
save sce with counts assay
```{r}
saveRDS(sce, "/mnt/central_nas/users/marllu/T_panel/data_analysis/sce_02_counts.rds")
```


To facilitate further downstream analysis, the non-compensated assays can now be
replaced by their compensated counterparts:

```{r overwrite-assays}
assay(sce, "counts") <- assay(sce, "compcounts") 
assay(sce, "exprs") <- assay(sce, "compexprs") 
assay(sce, "compcounts") <- assay(sce, "compexprs") <- NULL
```

# winsorize transformation
```{r}
assay(sce, "quant") <- t(apply(counts(sce), MARGIN = 1, function(x) winsorize(x,p=c(0,0.999))))
assay(sce, "exprs_quant") <-  asinh(assay(sce, "quant")/1)
assay(sce, "exprs_quant_5") <-  asinh(assay(sce, "quant")/5)

```

## Save objects

```{r save, message = F}
saveRDS(sce, "/mnt/central_nas/users/marllu/T_panel/data_analysis/sce_02.rds")
```
       
## Image compensation

The channelNames need to be set according to their metal isotope in the form (mt)(mass)Di and therefore match colnames(sm)
```{r}
channelNames(images) <- rowData(sce)$channel_name
```

The spillover matrix can now be adapted to exclude channels that were not kept for downstream analysis.
```{r}
adapted_sm <- adaptSpillmat(sm, channelNames(images), 
                            isotope_list = isotope_list)
```

```{r}
library(BiocParallel)

images_comp <- compImage(images[10:20], adapted_sm, 
                         BPPARAM = MulticoreParam())
```

```{r}
# Before compensation
plotPixels(images[17], colour_by = "Gd155Di" ,
           image_title = list(text = "Dy162 (CD45RO) - before", position = "topleft"), 
           legend = NULL, bcg = list(Gd155Di= c(0, 4, 1)))

plotPixels(images[17], colour_by = "La139Di", 
           image_title = list(text = "Dy163Di (FOXP3) - before", position = "topleft"), 
           legend = NULL, bcg = list(La139Di = c(0, 4, 1)))


# After compensation
plotPixels(images_comp[8], colour_by = "Gd155Di",
           image_title = list(text = "Dy162 (CD45RO) - after", position = "topleft"), 
           legend = NULL, bcg = list(Gd155Di = c(0, 4, 1)))

plotPixels(images_comp[8], colour_by = "La139Di", 
           image_title = list(text = "Dy163Di (FOXP3) - after", position = "topleft"),
           legend = NULL, bcg = list(La139Di = c(0, 4, 1)))


```


For convenience, we will re-set the channelNames to their biological targtes:
```{r}
channelNames(images) <- rownames(sce)
```
